input.question: What is the history of, and design conventions (if any), of album art?
input.ground_truth: If by album art you mean like for music CD's (or LP's and EP's back in the day), the history and design conventions are pretty broad. Some producers hire graphics artists or designers for their album covers, some artists make their own or have artistic friends make them. I'm not quite sure of the history in terms of when it began or what the first was, but I can point out a couple interesting design conventions from an art history standpoint! Franz Ferdinand. This indie Rock band has nearly all of their album designs based off of Soviet Constructivism: [album](_URL_6_) [painting](_URL_2_) [album](_URL_4_) [painting](_URL_3_) Coldplay: more mix in design, but [Viva la Vida](_URL_1_) features [Liberty Leading the People](_URL_5_) The Beatles: Their famous [Abbey Road](_URL_0_) cover was thought up by McCartney and professionally done. The photograph is not just a cover anymore, but part of British modern photography.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What is the history of, and design conventions (if any), of album art?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big box of crayons. Each crayon has its own wrapper, and sometimes the wrapper has a pretty picture on it to tell you what color the crayon is and make it look fun.

Long, long ago, when people listened to music on big round discs called "records," they started putting pictures on the front of those discs. These pictures are called "album art." At first, the pictures were just simple—maybe just the name of the music and the name of the singer. But soon, people started making the covers really cool and colorful, just like how you like your drawings!

As time went on, these music covers became like little pieces of art. Sometimes they showed what the music was about, like spaceships for a space song, or a sad face for a sad song. Sometimes they just looked cool or pretty.

Now, people put album art on CDs, cassette tapes, and even on the internet when you listen to music. Artists and designers work hard to make the covers look just right, so when you see the cover, you know what kind of music is inside.

So, the history is: People started putting pictures on music records, and now those pictures are called album art. The design rules are: Make it look interesting, tell something about the music, and make people want to look at it!
